feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain focus and solid progression at NACo. It reads professionally and shows scope well, but it is slightly repetitive, light on quantified outcomes beyond traffic/platform scale, and a bit overpacked with overlapping skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline and summary immediately establish a senior leader in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and public-sector communications.  
- Strong credibility and progression: long tenure at one organization with visible advancement from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Good evidence of scope: website scale, team/channel ownership, Drupal modernization, analytics stack, and AI search work all add impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome metrics: include results tied to redesigns, campaigns, newsletters, video, and analytics improvements (e.g., engagement, conversion, efficiency, adoption, cost/time savings).  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Tighten writing and consistency: some bullets are long and list-heavy. Standardize style choices such as “organization-wide” vs. “in-house,” and comma usage in series. No major misspellings or typos found; grammar is strong overall.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. Tightening it and adding one concrete signal of scale would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing web platforms, governance models, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise website transformation, analytics and reporting infrastructure, editorial workflows, multimedia production, and AI-enabled content discovery for complex, mission-driven organizations.
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct verbs like “modernizing,” “leading,” or “scaling” for stronger executive tone.
- Change “user experiences” to “content discovery” or “search experiences” to align more closely with the recent AI/search work in the CV.
- If space allows, add a scale cue such as “10,000+ page websites” or “multi-publisher environments” to increase specificity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- “Governance models,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong and relevant, but it overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership capabilities will make it feel more distinctive and executive-level.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, concise noun phrases and reduce repetition of “communications,” “operations,” and “systems.”
- Prioritize the most senior, differentiating strengths first: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search, automation.
- Consider this revision: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel digital communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space allows, replace “enterprise website modernization” with “enterprise web modernization” for cleaner style.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” overlaps with Topline Skills and Recent Projects; “content discovery” is a fresher angle.
- “Digital governance & editorial systems” and “Multi-channel communications operations” echo the header closely.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the block is dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding parallel structure will improve scanability and impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and distinguish this from core experience.
- Use consistent action/result structure, e.g., “Built/Developed [project] to [outcome],” and trim stacked nouns like “structured content workflows.”
- Make formatting more scannable with bullets instead of paragraph-style entries.
- Refine wording for style consistency: “10 x 20-foot” (not 10×20-foot), and consider “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current/previous NACo roles; keep this section brief and project-focused to avoid repeating Work Experience bullets.
- “Editorial storytelling,” “multimedia,” and “campaign” language also echoes other sections; emphasize distinct deliverables or outcomes here.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your NACo director role and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consulting value, senior advisory scope, and 2–3 concrete deliverables.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for enterprise communications.”
- Replace generic verbs (“consult,” “advise,” “deliver”) with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Designed,” “Implemented,” “Led,” “Streamlined,” “Launched.”
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets focused on distinct consulting contributions, e.g. platform/workflow modernization, campaign microsites/toolkits, AI search initiative, cross-channel governance.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, publishing efficiency gains, engagement improvements, search success metrics, or stakeholder/user adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, enterprise web improvement” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry; emphasize post-tenure consulting impact instead.
- Microsites and AI search also appear in Recent Projects, so keep this item higher-level and reserve feature detail for the project section.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with the earlier NACo role’s newsletter/video execution details.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget across enterprise communications.”
- Combine the website bullets into one impact-led line: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more outcome-focused: add growth, engagement, deliverability, production volume, or campaign results if available; otherwise shorten “reaching tens of thousands…” language.
- Tighten ops/analytics bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio” and “Expanded analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed email newsletters/social/video” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry at the strategic/enterprise level.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer project examples; keep the CV item focused on leadership and organizational impact.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads broad and overlaps with the more senior Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more execution-focused and quantify scale so it shows growth without repeating later leadership themes.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets and add outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders” and, if possible, add open rates, subscriber growth, or send volume.
- Reframe video bullet to show ownership: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Make coordination/workflow bullets more concrete: mention editorial calendar, cross-team approvals, publishing cadence, or process improvements that reduced turnaround time or improved consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthened editorial planning…” and “improved…publishing workflows” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- Weekly video work also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; emphasize scaling/formalizing the program here, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinct by emphasizing leadership scope and systems thinking over generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace with tighter, less overlapping bullets such as:
- Enterprise digital strategy and web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership for complex organizations
- Public-sector advocacy storytelling and audience strategy
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content operations” or “Publishing workflows” to better match recent leadership roles.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable scale for experience bullets rather than skills sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” duplicate both the header summary and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one version only.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and group tools under outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped, impact-oriented skills rather than a long platform list.
- Prioritize current/recent strengths: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations, automation.
- De-emphasize older/basic items like jQuery unless required by target roles.
- Suggested version:  
- Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization  
- Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript)  
- API integrations and workflow automation  
- SharePoint and Microsoft Power Pages  
- Airtable-based content and operational systems  
- AI-enabled search and discovery experiences

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal,” “WordPress,” “SharePoint,” and coding languages are already repeated in “Technical + IT”; keep this section higher-level.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating the exact phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. This Topline Skills item should emphasize strategic application, not repeat the stack.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first: “Analytics strategy, KPI framework design, executive reporting, user behavior analysis, SEO/performance optimization.”
- Keep only 3–4 flagship tools here and move the full stack to Technical + IT; e.g. “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI.”
- Tighten phrasing: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding and decision support.”
- Optional rewrite: “Analytics strategy & optimization — KPI framework design, executive dashboarding, user behavior analysis, SEO/performance optimization, powered by GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio and Power BI.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates the Technical + IT “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may also overlap with broader analytics claims in the Director of Digital Media entry.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and several NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and use sharper, more senior phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with a tighter, leadership-oriented list:
- Broadcast-quality video production
- Livestream and hybrid event delivery
- In-house studio operations
- PTZ camera and multi-camera workflows
- Consider “Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery” as the heading to better reflect the studio-build achievement.
- If space allows, swap “video production and editing” for “advocacy video programming” or “broadcast-quality video production” to sound more strategic and differentiated.
- Keep to 4 items max; this section should signal capability, not repeat task-level detail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” / “multimedia production” already appears in Core Competencies; vary wording here to avoid echo.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media studio bullet, so use this skills line to complement, not restate, that achievement.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, scannable list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. Since Drupal is central to the most recent roles, this item should better reflect depth and ordering by relevance.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recentest relevance: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider tightening the title to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show level of use: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If this section is meant to be purely technical, keep it platform-only and avoid mixing in broader capabilities already covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one instance or making this version more tool-specific.
- Drupal experience is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid overlisting it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools that support recent delivery work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Delivery**
- Reorder for relevance/recency: **JavaScript • HTML5/CSS3 • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • jQuery**
- Consider tightening older tech: move **jQuery** to the end or drop it if not central to current work.
- If space allows, add light specificity instead of pure tools: **JavaScript front-end implementation • API integrations • tag management • edge/serverless scripting • CI/CD automation**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**.
- “Google Tag Manager” may also overlap conceptually with analytics/tooling; keep it here only if positioned as implementation rather than reporting.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and grouped around systems you actually used most recently and strategically.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from a flat list to a tighter, role-relevant grouping: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana | Collaboration: Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Drop lower-value/general tools unless they were central recently; Basecamp and Trello feel dated versus your recent leadership roles.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier for impact: “Workflow automation, intake tracking, editorial coordination, and cross-team project management.”
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use “Microsoft Teams” instead of “Teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Airtable” and workflow automation already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same concept too many times.
- Jira/Asana/Slack/Teams are common workplace tools, so don’t let them crowd out more distinctive technical strengths.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. It should signal level of use and avoid repeating email leadership already covered in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- If accurate, add scope/strength signal: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (enterprise journeys, segmentation, automation) • Higher Logic (member communications) • Mailchimp**
- Order by strongest/recently relevant platform first; if Dynamics 365 is current or strategic, keep it first. If not, lead with the platform used most extensively.
- Use consistent naming: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys** rather than the slash format for cleaner ATS/readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Your work experience already shows strong email-channel leadership; don’t add generic phrases like “email campaigns” here unless you specify platform capability.
- If Higher Logic or Mailchimp were only light exposure, consider removing one to keep this section credible and concise.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and the NACo work bullets. Use it to sharpen technical specificity rather than restating broad capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with a tighter, tool-first list: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting**
- Consider swapping **SEO** for **Google Search Console** or **technical SEO analysis**; “SEO” is too broad for a technical tools section.
- Replace **Dashboarding** with **KPI reporting** or **analytics infrastructure** if you want a more senior, outcomes-linked phrase.
- If space allows, order by strongest/recently used tools first: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity...**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; keep this section strictly tool/platform focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid adding generic descriptors here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to foundational team-building, production, and platform support.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer action/result language: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand the organization’s in-house publishing capacity.”
- Tighten the management point: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “mentored a junior digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the later “weekly advocacy video update”; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating broad “web, email, social, video” leadership language already covered more strongly in 2018–2024 roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later multimedia/digital content roles. Tighten it to emphasize innovation/program support plus the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Cut generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a more specific verb such as “produced” or “developed” only if accurate.
- If possible, add scope or result: number of episodes, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content supported member engagement or policy communications.
- Keep this entry to 1 sentence or 2 short bullets since later roles already show broader digital leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later video/multimedia entries; avoid repeating that theme here unless tied to a distinct outcome.
- Podcast production is the most unique element in this role—make it the anchor.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads more like a mixed capability list than a tight tools section. It also overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills, so keep this entry software/tool-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream production systems • Podcast recording/editing**
- Replace “Livestream studio workflows” with “Livestream production systems” or specific tools/platforms if available; “workflows” is vague for a technical skills list.
- Make phrasing parallel: use either all tools or all capabilities; if these are true hands-on skills, “Podcast recording/editing” is stronger than the broader “Podcast production.”
- If space allows and accurate, add one concrete platform/tool used in studio work to increase credibility.
